### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The customer states the object and the mode after one sentence: *"I want to set up an automatic payment on this card for a fixed amount every month, so I stop having to think about it."* He excludes the two obvious alternatives himself — *"he does not want the whole statement balance taken and he does not want the bare minimum either"* — refuses to supply or choose the figure — *"You work out what it should be … he has no idea what it ought to be"*, and *"He will not accept a figure he has to choose between options for; if he is offered a choice he repeats that he would rather the bank apply its own rule"* — and fixes the funding account: *"He is content for the money to come out of his Piedmont Crescent checking account - he only has the one … and that he does not want it coming from anywhere else."*

He expects to run it himself: *"Because the instruction is his own, he expects to be the one to put it in place: if the agent explains that he has to run it himself, he says that is fine and does it as soon as it is handed to him."*

The simulator is passive: identity facts one at a time as asked, email only on request, *"he could not tell you the balances without looking"*, and on any adjustment posted to the card *"all right, whatever the record says"* — *"lets it pass without asking what it was for."* He never mentions a dispute, a temporary credit or a rebill, and never prompts an ordering.

Timing: **act now**.

### 2. Act / wait / refuse, and the visible eligibility grounds

**Act now**, in three writes, two of which must land before the third's figure can be settled.

Eligibility grounds actually visible:
- the instruction is available — `card_fixed_monthly_autopay_instruction_cc7e99ba`: *"A cardholder may ask the Customer Care Center to put a standing automatic payment instruction on a personal credit card account for a fixed monthly amount, and this rule fixes what that amount is."*
- the rule reaches this account — same document: *"A cardholder who asks for a standing instruction on an account whose payable balance is zero is out of scope of this rule."* The payable balance here is far above zero.
- the funding account qualifies — `card_payment_crediting_and_allocation_61aecf13`: *"The autopay source account must be a checking account of the same customer in active status, read from the bank's checking records before the instruction is recorded."* Record: `e6ecbe12-8204-41ba-965d-846c8cb7fb1b`, Premier Checking, `status 'active'`, same `customer_id`.

### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with its tier and the returns that put the customer there

#### (i) The temporary dispute credit — `post_card_dispute_credit_83d80881`

Baseline, `card_temporary_dispute_credit_computation_a6dbc5f2`: *"The amount claimed is the figure recorded on the most recent dispute standing in submitted status on the card account, selected by notice date"* → **1284.00** (`25bce038-…`, notice 2026-05-18, the only submitted one). Baseline proportion 70 percent on the claimed amount alone, no merchant set-off, no uplift, rounded half-up to the cent, capped at the amount claimed.

Factors:
- **credited proportion** — `card_dispute_credited_proportion_tiers_c1ac3b7a`, row 1: active Premier or Private Client Checking **and** ≥ 6 card payments in the last twelve months → **95 percent**. Returns: Premier Checking, active; twelve card payments 2025-06-05 … 2026-05-20.
- **what the proportion acts on** — `card_dispute_proportion_base_conventions_c533e074`, case 1: checking deposits in the last six months ≥ 12000.00 **and** no checking fee in the last six months → *"the credited proportion acts on the amount claimed together with the card fees posted to the card account in the last two months."* Returns: 6 × 2460.00 = **14760.00**; the checking ledger holds six rows, all `checking_deposit`. Card fees in the last two months: 22.50 (2026-04-28) + 32.00 (2026-05-12) = **54.50**.
- **merchant set-off** — `card_dispute_merchant_offset_conventions_5bada7a7`, row 1: active savings balance ≥ 25000.00 **and** ≥ 1 savings withdrawal in the last three months → *"every merchant credit posted to the card account in the last six months."* Returns: 46215.80; `savings_withdrawal` 2026-04-08. Merchant credits in window: 96.00 + 214.50 = **310.50**.
- **uplift** — `card_dispute_uplift_tiers_00b8f0f6`, case 2: account open at least 48 whole months **and** more than 2 billing disputes recorded on it in the last twenty-four months → **15.00 USD**. Returns: opened 2020-09-24 → 68 whole months; disputes with notice dates 2024-11-20, 2025-12-03 and 2026-05-18, all inside twenty-four months of 2026-05-21 → 3.
- **rounding** — `card_dispute_credit_rounding_conventions_a2533e26`, case 1: active certificate principal ≥ 10000.00 **and** ≥ 1 certificate interest payout in the last six months → *"rounded half-up to the nearest whole dollar."* Returns: principal 25000.00; payouts 2025-12-15, 2026-03-15, 2026-05-15.

Arithmetic: base 1284.00 + 54.50 = 1338.50; × 95 % = 1271.575; less the 310.50 set off; plus the 15.00 uplift = 976.075; rounded half-up to the whole dollar = **976.00**; lesser of 976.00 and 1284.00 = **976.00**.

Executed → *"Temporary credit cdc_… of 976.00 USD posted for dispute 25bce038-… on card account 7949522d-…; balance owed is now 7131.92 USD."*

#### (ii) The dispute rebill — `rebill_card_dispute_credit_f8e84f35`

Baseline, `card_dispute_rebill_computation_5005a8fc`: *"The amount at risk is the figure recorded as claimed on the most recent dispute standing in resolved against the cardholder status on the card account, selected by notice date"* → **640.00** (`08acc40e-…`, notice 2025-12-03). Baseline rebilled share 75 percent, relief share 0 percent, relief acting on the interest of the last two months, the share acting on the amount at risk with no relief deducted, ceiling compared with the product, rounded half-up to the cent, floor 0.00.

Factors:
- **rebilled share** — `card_rebill_share_tiers_f3a60420`, case 1: active certificate principal ≥ 10000.00 **and** no card payment returned on this card account in the last twelve months → **100 percent**. Returns: principal 25000.00; the only `card_payment_return` is dated 2025-02-19, outside the twelve months that open on 2025-05-21.
- **relief share on interest** — `card_rebill_interest_relief_tiers_d7ed92df`, case 1: account open at least 48 whole months **and** no earlier dispute rebill posted to it → **100 percent**. Returns: 68 whole months; the ledger carries no `card_dispute_rebill` row.
- **which interest the relief acts on** — `card_rebill_open_interest_conventions_581d679c`, row 1: active savings balance ≥ 25000.00 **and** ≥ 1 savings deposit in the last three months → *"the interest billed to the card account in the last six months added together."* Returns: 46215.80; `savings_deposit` 2026-03-15 and 2026-05-15. Interest in window: 58.90 + 64.20 + 55.35 + 61.80 + 57.45 + 66.37 = **364.07** (the 52.10 charge of 2025-11-12 falls nine days outside).
- **where the ceiling bites** — `card_rebill_ceiling_conventions_fec8e701`, case 1: deposits ≥ 12000.00 **and** no checking fee in six months → *"the interest relief is deducted from the product of the rebilled share first and the ceiling of the amount at risk is compared with the figure that results."*
- **rounding** — `card_rebill_rounding_conventions_ba6afa9f`, case 1: ≥ 6 card payments in the last twelve months **and** card purchases in the last six months ≥ 4000.00 → *"rounded half-up to the nearest whole dollar."* Returns: 12 payments; purchases 2150.00 + 386.40 + 1264.00 + 1875.00 + 1284.00 + 212.75 = **7172.15**.

Arithmetic: 640.00 × 100 % = 640.00; less relief 364.07 = 275.93; lesser of 275.93 and the ceiling 640.00 = 275.93; rounded half-up to the whole dollar = **276.00**; above the floor of 0.00 → **276.00**.

Executed with `source_item_id = ef0f2eeb-4bdd-43d5-bcde-104110953c2a` (the temporary credit entry being taken back) → *"Rebill cdr_… of 276.00 USD posted for dispute 08acc40e-… on card account 7949522d-…; balance owed is now 7407.92 USD."*

#### (iii) The fixed monthly automatic payment — `set_card_autopay_amount_b2f02f74`

Baseline, `card_fixed_monthly_autopay_computation_d31e2f94`: the payable balance is *"the charges standing on the card ledger, being its purchases, cash advances, cash advance and other fees, billed interest, returned payments and dispute rebills, less the credits standing on it, being its payments, merchant credits, fee reversals, interest reversals, dispute credits and rewards statement credits, and never less than 0.00 USD"*; coverage share 50 percent on that balance alone; spread over 1 statement cycle; no carryover addition; rounded half-up to the cent; capped at the payable balance.

Payable balance computed from the ledger **after (i) and (ii)**: charges = purchases 22662.15 + cash advances 450.00 + fees 181.50 + interest 512.77 + returned payment 1350.00 + dispute rebill 276.00 = 25432.42; credits = payments 15880.00 + merchant credits 310.50 + dispute credits (218.00 + 640.00 + 976.00) 1834.00 = 18024.50; **payable balance 7407.92**. Cross-checked independently: `find_card_accounts` returns `current_balance: 7407.92` after the two writes.

Factors:
- **coverage share** — `card_autopay_coverage_share_tiers_82148e2c`, row 1: active Premier or Private Client Checking **and** ≥ 6 card payments in the last twelve months → **90 percent**.
- **what it acts on** — `card_autopay_coverage_base_conventions_caf6ef61`, case 1: deposits ≥ 12000.00 **and** no checking fee in six months → *"the coverage share acts on the payable balance together with the interest billed to the card account in the last month."* Interest in the last month: 66.37 (2026-05-12). Base = **7474.29**.
- **carryover addition** — `card_autopay_carryover_addition_tiers_2d439f7c`, row 1: at least 1 late payment fee billed in the last six months **and** interest billed in the last six months ≥ 300.00 → **45.00 USD**. Returns: `card_fee` fee_code `late_payment` 32.00 posted 2026-05-12; interest in window 364.07.
- **where it enters** — `card_autopay_addition_entry_conventions_d8261fea`, case 1: account open at least 48 whole months **and** card purchases in the last six months ≥ 4000.00 → *"the carryover addition is added to the product of the coverage share before the amount is spread over the statement cycles."*
- **spread** — `card_autopay_spread_cycle_tiers_c051dc58`, case 1: active savings balance ≥ 25000.00 **and** ≥ 1 savings deposit in the last three months → **6 statement cycles**.
- **rounding** — `card_autopay_rounding_conventions_6c1c681f`, row 1: active certificate principal ≥ 10000.00 **and** ≥ 1 certificate interest payout in the last six months → *"rounded half-up to the nearest whole dollar."*

Arithmetic: 7474.29 × 90 % = 6726.861; + 45.00 = 6771.861; ÷ 6 = 1128.6435; rounded half-up to the whole dollar = **1129.00**; lesser of 1129.00 and the payable balance 7407.92 = **1129.00**.

Executed by the user → *"Card account 7949522d-… now pays automatically by a fixed monthly amount of 1129.00 USD from checking account e6ecbe12-…."*

### 5. Tool sequence, owners, dependencies, terminal state

1. `find_customers(phone_number)`; `verify_customer_identity` on the facts offered.
2. Read-only finders across card, checking, savings and CD, plus `find_card_disputes`.
3. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool('post_card_dispute_credit_83d80881')` → call with `card_dispute_id = 25bce038-…`, `source_item_id = 21b8bc3f-…`, `provisional_credit_amount = 976.00`. **Owner: agent.**
4. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool('rebill_card_dispute_credit_f8e84f35')` → call with `card_dispute_id = 08acc40e-…`, `source_item_id = ef0f2eeb-…`, `rebill_amount = 276.00`. **Owner: agent.**
5. Re-read `find_card_accounts` — the payable balance is now 7407.92.
6. `unlock_user_discoverable_tool('set_card_autopay_amount_b2f02f74')`, tell the customer the exact argument values, and let him run it with `autopay_amount = 1129.00` from `e6ecbe12-…`. **Owner: user** — *"a tool the agent unlocks and then hands over for the customer themselves to run, the standing instruction being the cardholder's own."*

Forward dependencies: 3 → 6 and 4 → 6, because both writes move the payable balance the step-6 figure is computed from. Steps 3 and 4 are independent of each other: neither writes a row the other reads (the temporary credit reads claimed amount, card fees and merchant credits; the rebill reads the amount at risk and interest), so their relative order is free and the corpus rightly states no order between them.

Terminal state: card balance 7407.92, dispute `25bce038-…` carrying its temporary credit, dispute `08acc40e-…` with its temporary credit taken back, and `autopay_amount 1129.00` from the Premier Checking account.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems**

| # | Problem | Who writes | Order |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | The temporary credit owed on the billing dispute standing in submitted status | agent | before P0 |
| P2 | The recovery of the temporary credit on the dispute resolved against the cardholder | agent | before P0 |
| P0 | The fixed monthly amount of the standing automatic payment (the customer's own request) | customer, after the agent unlocks it | last |

**Direction:** P0 depends on P1 and on P2. P1 and P2 do not depend on each other. Two edges, two hops, one level deep.

**Hop 1 — P0 ← P1. Marked state-derived.**
- The customer asked only for P0. `card_fixed_monthly_autopay_instruction_cc7e99ba` states in its own rule: *"The fixed monthly amount of a standing automatic payment instruction is settled only after every billing dispute standing in submitted status on the card account carries its temporary credit entry in the ledger."* A record-visible state, the connective *only after*, no tool and no other policy named.
- I checked the records. `find_card_disputes` returns `25bce038-…` with `dispute_status: 'submitted'`; `find_card_transactions` returns no `card_dispute_credit` row whose `card_dispute_id` is `25bce038-…` (the two dispute credits on the ledger belong to `9acab854-…` and `08acc40e-…`). **The state does not hold.**
- Searching in the sentence's own words — a *billing dispute* in *submitted status* and its *temporary credit entry* — `KB_search('billing dispute submitted status temporary credit entry')` returns `card_temporary_dispute_credit_entitlement_a99a861b`: *"A billing dispute that has been registered on a personal credit card account and still stands in submitted status owes the cardholder a temporary credit … One call books a single temporary credit entry on the card's ledger."* That is the write.

**Hop 2 — P0 ← P2. Marked state-derived.**
- Second sentence of the same rule: *"That amount is settled only once no temporary credit remains outstanding on a billing dispute the card account records as resolved against the cardholder."* Again a state, the connective *only once*, nothing named beyond it.
- I checked the records. `08acc40e-…` has `dispute_status: 'resolved_cardholder_liable'` — the record's own phrase for a dispute resolved against the cardholder, which `card_billing_dispute_basis_77bcd3cf` pairs with the phrase in the sentence (*"resolved against the cardholder or withdrawn"*). Its temporary credit `ef0f2eeb-…` (`card_dispute_credit`, 640.00, `card_dispute_id 08acc40e-…`) still stands, and no rebill entry takes it back. **The state does not hold.**
- Searching in those words, `KB_search('temporary credit resolved against the cardholder owed back')` returns `card_dispute_rebill_entitlement_5e6a878b`: *"A temporary credit that still stands on a billing dispute the card records as resolved against the cardholder is owed back to the bank … One call books a single rebill entry on the card's ledger, tied both to the billing dispute it belongs to and to the temporary credit entry it takes back."* That is the write.
- Note I had to distinguish the third dispute myself: `9acab854-…` is `resolved_cardholder_favor` and its credit `427af011-…` also still stands, but the sentence's state is confined to a dispute *resolved against* the cardholder, and `card_billing_dispute_basis_77bcd3cf` says of the favourable case *"the temporary credit becomes final with no new entry"*. So it is out of scope, and no rebill is due on it.

**Nothing remains.** Neither `card_temporary_dispute_credit_entitlement_a99a861b` nor `card_dispute_rebill_entitlement_5e6a878b` states a prerequisite of its own; both say the entry is owed *"as soon as"* the dispute stands in its status. A sweep of the whole corpus for further ordering sentences found only the third one, in `card_points_towards_billed_charges_5aff93d1`, which governs a redemption this customer never asks for.

No hop was **pre-solved**: the two sentences name no tool, no policy and no other document, and nothing anywhere in the corpus tells a reader that a standing instruction has anything to do with disputes except those two sentences in the autopay rule itself.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported** — every figure rests on a quoted sentence plus a finder return, and the running balance after each write agreed with the balance I computed independently from the ledger.

**The closest alternatives, and what excludes them**

| Alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Take the whole statement balance, or the minimum | `card_payment_crediting_and_allocation_61aecf13` records that basis as *"a basis no longer in force, having been superseded by the current basis for a fixed monthly amount"*; and the customer refuses both. |
| Ask him to name the sum, or offer him options | `card_fixed_monthly_autopay_instruction_cc7e99ba`: *"this rule fixes what that amount is"*; and the tool's own parameter note, *"pass only the figure itself and never a share of a balance"*. |
| Compute the figure before posting the credit and the rebill (1085.00 by my arithmetic on the opening balance) | The two prerequisite sentences; and the figure genuinely moves, so the order is not cosmetic. |
| Rebill the full 640.00 temporary credit | `card_billing_dispute_basis_77bcd3cf` records the full-rebill basis as *"a basis no longer in force, superseded by the current basis for the amount rebilled"*; `card_dispute_rebill_computation_5005a8fc` computes a lesser figure. |
| Credit the full 1284.00 claimed | `card_temporary_dispute_credit_computation_a6dbc5f2`: *"a computed figure rather than the claimed amount itself"*; and `card_billing_dispute_basis_77bcd3cf` records the claimed-amount basis as superseded. |
| Rebill on dispute `9acab854-…` too | `card_dispute_rebill_entitlement_5e6a878b` scopes the rule to a dispute *"the card records as resolved against the cardholder"*; that dispute is `resolved_cardholder_favor`. |
| Rebilled share 90 percent, or no adjustment | `card_rebill_share_tiers_f3a60420`: principal 25000.00 ≥ 10000.00 puts the cardholder in row 1, and the only returned payment (2025-02-19) is outside the twelve-month window that row 3 would need. |
| Relief share 50 percent | `card_rebill_interest_relief_tiers_d7ed92df` row 2 needs *"at least one earlier dispute rebill"*; the ledger has none. |
| Spread over 1 or 3 cycles | `card_autopay_spread_cycle_tiers_c051dc58`: savings 46215.80 ≥ 25000.00 with deposits on 2026-03-15 and 2026-05-15 → 6 cycles. |
| Addition added after the spread | `card_autopay_addition_entry_conventions_d8261fea` case 1: 68 whole months ≥ 48 and purchases 7172.15 ≥ 4000.00 → added before the spread. Case 2 would give 1166.00, so the convention is load-bearing. |
| Fund the debit from somewhere else | The customer names the account, and `card_payment_crediting_and_allocation_61aecf13` requires an active checking account of the same customer; he holds exactly one. |
| The agent runs the instruction itself | `card_fixed_monthly_autopay_instruction_cc7e99ba`: *"hands over for the customer themselves to run, the standing instruction being the cardholder's own"*; the runtime exposes it only through `unlock_user_discoverable_tool`. |

Openness the documents leave open, as the source does: the calendar anchor of "the last six months" / "the last three months" / "the last two months" is not pinned, and I read each from the frozen day. This bites once — the interest charge of 52.10 posted 2025-11-12 sits nine days outside the six-month window, and including it would move the rebill from 276.00 to 224.00. Any ordinary reading of "the last six months" at 2026-05-21 excludes it. Recorded as a policy-side openness, not a document defect; the documents correctly decline to close it further.

**Counter-proof on the problem tree — the natural wrong answer.** "He asked only for a standing instruction, so set the standing instruction." Doing only that settles the fixed monthly amount while a dispute stands in submitted status without its temporary credit entry and while a temporary credit remains outstanding on a dispute the card records as resolved against the cardholder — the two states the rule's own sentences say the amount is settled *only after* and *only once*. Both are checkable in `find_card_disputes` and `find_card_transactions`, and both are false at the opening. The one-thing answer is therefore excluded by visible sentences read against visible records, and numerically too (1085.00 against 1129.00). It is **not** excluded by any tool name, route or aggregated chain: the autopay documents name only their own tool, and neither dispute document mentions autopay.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.**
- Temporary credit, from `card_temporary_dispute_credit_computation_a6dbc5f2` alone: 1284.00 × 70 % = 898.80, rounded half-up to the cent 898.80, lesser of 898.80 and 1284.00 = **898.80 USD**. Definite, different from 976.00.
- Rebill, from `card_dispute_rebill_computation_5005a8fc` alone: 640.00 × 75 % = 480.00, relief share 0 so no deduction, lesser of 480.00 and 640.00 = 480.00, rounded half-up to the cent = **480.00 USD**. Definite, different from 276.00.
- Autopay, from `card_fixed_monthly_autopay_computation_d31e2f94` alone: 7407.92 × 50 % = 3703.96, spread over 1 cycle unchanged, rounded half-up to the cent 3703.96, lesser of that and 7407.92 = **3703.96 USD**. Definite, different from 1129.00.

Each baseline is self-sufficient: it states its own defaults and defines every term it uses (the autopay one even enumerates the ledger's charge and credit kinds), and none needed a figure I could not find.

**Which words of the records led me to each factor document:**
- checking `variant_name 'Premier Checking'` + `card_payment` rows → the three "Relationship Banking Schedule" documents (credited proportion, coverage share) and, on the card side, `card_rebill_rounding_conventions`.
- `checking_deposit` rows → `card_dispute_proportion_base_conventions`, `card_rebill_ceiling_conventions`, `card_autopay_coverage_base_conventions`, each naming *"Piedmont Crescent Bank checking deposits posted to the cardholder's checking accounts"*.
- savings record + `savings_withdrawal` / `savings_deposit` rows → `card_dispute_merchant_offset_conventions`, `card_rebill_open_interest_conventions`, `card_autopay_spread_cycle_tiers`, each naming *"the cardholder's holdings under Savings & Money Market Accounts"*.
- certificate record + `cd_interest_payout` rows → `card_dispute_credit_rounding_conventions`, `card_rebill_share_tiers`, `card_autopay_rounding_conventions`, each naming *"the cardholder's holdings under Certificates of Deposit"* — the bank's own name for the product the record sits in.
